items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1957-03-26
items.q: Mary Brunus, Denise, Abby Brunus, Georgie Brunus.

ctx.x: Who's that? He looks familiar. Mary Brunus. Oh, that's Mary.
Mary Brunus, Denise, Abby Brunus, Georgie Brunus.
It looks like they got a bottle of muscatel. That Harry Shields?

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine, Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine and Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1959-02-27
items.q: And Haley Brunus, and Georgie Brunus, and Merit Brunus, and Abby Brunus, and had Kaz Out. Oh, yeah, Jones Kaz Out. All them kids, you know, brothers, they played music. And I stood right between them and told them how to come down.

ctx.x: Jimmy Kennell. He played cornet too. He played with him too?

I was over, this was around about 1910. Somewhere along around 1910. I was in Biloxi. I had three bands in Biloxi. I had a junior band playing for the junior company. I had one for the West End and one for a volunteer. Three bands. Well, I had all kids. All youngsters ranged in Biloxi, I guess they'd say, from about 16 years down to eight. I had 14 pieces in that band. Mississippi Hook and Ladder was right across the park where we were in, what's the name, Kennedy's Hotel. The park was like here, Kennedy's Hotel…
They played all them halls, the Portuguese and the Washington of Terror, the out- I don't think- All that used to always have ordainances, you know, balls and all.

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23
items.q: Well, he sends Abby Brunus in each place to play that carnival parade.

ctx.x: Yes. And, uh, of course, it happened to be close to a Mardi Gras. And I had three bands out that year. And, uh, well, little Brunus, Abby, he was a pretty fair corner player. It was then at that time, too. He was picking up mighty nice, very nice. Well, he sends Abby Brunus in each place to play that carnival parade. While he went around scouting, I guess, to get members to go north with, see? Now, he claims he went first there, to went up north first. No. I believe Tom Brown was a man who went up north first. I…
I believe he went a year before or so.

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1964-04-25
items.q: I took them all in the band. And I'll tell you about the Brunish boys.

ctx.x: I took them all in the band. And I'll tell you about the Brunish boys. The daddy was a good musicianer, good violin player, mighty good violin player. And he loved music. He sure loved music. That old man sure loved music. So he'd get them kids all together, he's kids, buy them old instruments and stuff, and practice. And get out on the street with them kids. Is that right? On the street and play at the corners. If you give them nickels, all right, if you didn't, it was all right too. That was old man, brother.
Fine old dance. Did you ever play the Lusitanus Hall? Oh my God. Yeah. Where was that at?
